newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor sees progress in rent control talks.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor sees progress in rent control talks.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said he saw progress in talks to extend rent controls with legislative leaders.

"We also tried to be helpful to the extent that we could in encouraging more private discussion between the speaker and the majority leader so that they can find some common ground on this, and we think we've made progress in that area," said Giuliani, who on Monday campaigned in Albany to extend rent controls that affect nearly one million apartments in the city. He made his remarks to reporters in Albany.
City Council Speaker Peter Vallone, a Democrat, joined the Republican mayor in urging Albany lawmakers to develop a compromise.
However, Giuliani's optimism was countered by aides to both Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, and Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, the New York Times reported Tuesday.
The aides for both to the two lawmakers told the paper their leaders had not retreated at all from their positions and that no compromise was in sight.

Bruno is pushing to end rent controls that mainly affect New York City residents in two years, while keeping protections for the needy, disabled and elderly. Silver, in contrast, wants the rules, which expire on June 15, extended.
Giuliani suggested a possible compromise, perhaps including more state aid for building new housing, according to the paper.
A spokesman for Bruno said the senator felt it was positive that he did have some dialog with Giuliani and Silver.
A spokeswoman for Silver was not immediately available to comment.
